parsed.title: Which Scholars Accept the Facts for the Resurrection? - Gary Habermas
parsed.summary: Habermas answers the objection that minimal-facts consensus is biased because the scholars surveyed are Christians. He counters that he deliberately weights toward liberal/critical scholars (Bultmann, Jesus Seminar, Dunn, Flew), that criteria require a terminal degree plus publication in the field, and that even hostile scholars concede the six facts and early Jerusalem-church traditions.

atoms.name: Minimal-facts consensus is not a Christian bias artifact
atoms.statementTechnical: The scholarly consensus on the six minimal resurrection facts is not explained by the religious commitment of the surveyed scholars, since the same facts are affirmed by non-Christian and far-left critical scholars (Bultmann, Flew, Jesus Seminar contributors).
atoms.statementPlain: The six facts aren't just agreed on by Christians; even atheist and very liberal scholars grant them.
atoms.falsificationCondition: A representative survey of critical resurrection scholars showing the six facts are affirmed only by self-identified Christians, or that non-Christian specialists deny them at high rates.
atoms.notes: Core rebuttal to the 'biased sample' objection.

atoms.name: Bultmann affirms a pre-Markan passion narrative and early Jerusalem-church sayings
atoms.statementTechnical: Rudolf Bultmann, though far left of Ehrman, accepts a pre-Markan passion narrative and holds that early sayings go back to the very earliest Jerusalem church, and in his 1941 essay states the earliest disciples preached the resurrection.
atoms.statementPlain: Even Bultmann, a very skeptical scholar, admitted early sources and that the first disciples preached Jesus was raised.
atoms.falsificationCondition: Show Bultmann's texts deny a pre-Markan source or deny that the earliest disciples preached the resurrection; or show the cited passages are misattributed.

atoms.name: Criteria for a 'critical scholar' = terminal degree + field competence/publication
atoms.statementTechnical: A qualifying critical scholar has a terminal degree (PhD, D.Theol., D.Phil.) and works in a relevant field (NT, OT, history, philosophy, archaeology, world religions), with allowances for non-PhD researchers who demonstrably know the data.
atoms.statementPlain: To count, a scholar needs a doctorate in a relevant area and real knowledge of the research.
atoms.falsificationCondition: Demonstrate that Habermas's published volumes in fact include unqualified scholars by his own stated criteria, or that the criteria are applied inconsistently.

atoms.name: Habermas's survey is deliberately slanted toward liberal scholars
atoms.statementTechnical: Habermas states in his book's introduction that his selection is slanted toward liberal scholars, and he is more lenient with liberals than conservatives, to preempt the bias charge.
atoms.statementPlain: He intentionally includes more skeptical/liberal scholars than conservative ones.
atoms.falsificationCondition: Show the published volumes are in fact dominated by conservative/evangelical scholars, contradicting the stated slant.

atoms.name: Jesus Seminar presupposes 'dead men don't rise'
atoms.statementTechnical: The Jesus Seminar's two volumes open with ~38-39 presuppositions, one of which is that dead men do not rise, so the resurrected Jesus has no words in the Gospels.
atoms.statementPlain: The Jesus Seminar began by assuming resurrections don't happen, so their conclusions were pre-loaded.
atoms.falsificationCondition: Show the Jesus Seminar's stated presuppositions do not include a no-resurrection premise, or that the cited passage is misread.
atoms.notes: Used to show even hostile scholars concede data.

atoms.name: Targeting publishing scholars yields informed opinions
atoms.statementTechnical: Restricting the consensus survey to scholars who publish on resurrection research is justified because only they hold informed opinions; uninformed PhDs (e.g., Egyptologists, documentary historians) are irrelevant.
atoms.statementPlain: Only scholars who actually study and publish on the resurrection have opinions worth counting.
atoms.falsificationCondition: Show that non-publishing specialists in adjacent fields systematically disagree with the minimal facts, undermining the informed-opinion restriction.
atoms.notes: Answers the 'why not all scholars' objection.

atoms.name: Consensus is biased because the sample is Christian
atoms.statementTechnical: Objection: the minimal-facts consensus is an artifact of sampling scholars who are already Christians and thus committed to the conclusion.
atoms.statementPlain: You only get agreement because you're asking Christians.

atoms.name: Consensus ignores scholars who don't publish in the field
atoms.statementTechnical: Objection: a scholarly-consensus argument is invalid if it surveys only the subset of scholars who publish in the literature rather than all scholars.
atoms.statementPlain: You're cherry-picking by only counting published specialists.

atoms.name: Antony Flew accepted all 12 facts as an atheist
atoms.statementTechnical: In a debate, the moderator listed 12 facts and Antony Flew, then the best-known philosophical atheist, accepted all 12.
atoms.statementPlain: A famous atheist philosopher agreed with all twelve facts in a debate.

atoms.name: Raymond Brown reproduces Soards' list of scholars accepting a pre-Markan source
atoms.statementTechnical: In the appendix to Raymond Brown's two-volume The Death of the Messiah, Soards' essay lists critical scholars (including Bultmann) who accept a pre-Markan passion narrative possibly predating AD 37.
atoms.statementPlain: A top Catholic scholar's appendix lists many critical scholars who accept an early Markan source.

atoms.name: Christians deny the empty tomb, showing data-driven method
atoms.statementTechnical: If Christian scholars simply rubber-stamped Christian conclusions, the empty tomb would be a minimal fact; since many Christians deny it, their conclusions track the data.
atoms.statementPlain: Christians disagree with each other on the empty tomb, so they aren't just toeing a party line.

atoms.name: Caption noise and speaker-label gaps
atoms.statementTechnical: Auto-caption artifacts, missing speaker labels, and unclear date references (Strauss death year '72/'71/'1772').
atoms.notes: Not a claim; flagged for cleanup.
